Anthropic mathematician says Claude helped prove Riemann hypothesis

Category: AI

Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he used the company’s Claude model to develop a proof of the Riemann hypothesis. The claim remains subject to scrutiny. He says the approach also proves the broader Generalized Riemann Hypothesis. Alpöge said he chose the research direction, while Claude made rapid technical advances near the end; the model worked as a collaborator rather than solving the problem on its own [21][64][63]. The argument is available as computer-checkable Lean code rather than a conventional paper. Independent mathematicians, including Massachusetts Institute of Technology mathematician Andrew Sutherland, have compiled and rechecked the code with Lean’s kernel. Those checks verify the formalized reasoning but do not by themselves establish whether the encoded theorem matches the intended conjecture or explain the proof’s ideas to mathematicians [53][44]. Alpöge says he has not yet mastered all the mathematics involved and plans to explain the work and write it up. Mathematicians expect review and comprehension to take time [3][29][41].

What I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater.

— Levent Alpöge, Anthropic mathematician (Gizmodo)

Did you know: The Riemann hypothesis had already been checked for the first 10 trillion relevant zeros, according to the Clay Mathematics Institute description cited by Tom’s Hardware [11].

Key Points

  • Prior dispute: Alpöge and New York University mathematician Tristan Buckmaster questioned whether their research on fluid equations informed OpenAI’s Navier–Stokes work; OpenAI denied wrongdoing [29][25].
  • October follow-up: OpenAI released what it described as solutions, proofs or major advances on 372 additional problems in advanced mathematics; experts were expected to need months or longer to review them [86].
  • Human interpretation: Mathematicians expect that making the code understandable to humans could take years [101].
  • Earlier progress: In August, Anthropic said an unreleased version of Claude raised a lower bound on the share of Riemann zeta-function zeros on the critical line from 41.6% to 67.2%, while stressing that it had not proved the hypothesis [42][87].
  • Earlier progress: In August, Anthropic said an unreleased version of Claude raised a lower bound on the share of relevant zeta-function zeros on the predicted line from 41.6% to 67.2%, while explicitly stopping short of proving the hypothesis [7].
  • Human-only claim: After Alpöge’s announcement, Stanford postdoctoral researcher Alessandro Masullo released a separate, AI-free proof draft that he said he had developed over 12 years. He warned that it could contain errors because he had rushed publication [61].
  • AI research debate: A group of mathematics scholars argued that AI companies’ public claims of major solutions to promote commercial systems were “detrimental to the science of mathematics” [86].
  • AI research context: OpenAI’s September claim of an AI-generated solution to the Navier-Stokes problem had already prompted disputes over research credit, including objections from mathematician Tristan Buckmaster, who had worked with Alpöge on related research into fluid equations [29][54].
  • Announcement timing: Alpöge said he consulted Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei before announcing the result and acknowledged that the timing could be viewed cynically, without elaborating [29].
  • Human claim: Masullo said his separate, AI-free effort took 12 years; Vakil posted the current draft rather than wait for a planned year of polishing and further review [44][99].

Perspectives

Andrew Sutherland, MIT mathematician: Sutherland said independent checks compiled the Lean proof using only three standard axioms, but those checks do not replace mathematical examination of the theorem the code proves [53].

Steven Strogatz, Cornell mathematics professor: Strogatz said that if the proof holds up, it would be an extremely big deal, calling the Riemann hypothesis “the Moby Dick of Mathematics” [41].

Sources: Business Insider

Andrew Sutherland, MIT research scientist: Sutherland said he was both nervous and excited about the future, calling the announcement a day for celebration while acknowledging concerns about AI’s impact on mathematical work [6].

Nestor Guillén, NYU visiting mathematics professor: Guillén said he was glad this case might avoid the corporate controversy around Navier–Stokes and praised Alpöge’s openness about not fully understanding the proof, describing AI’s role as more like a tool [73].

Sources: The Straits Times

Group of mathematics scholars: The scholars warned that AI firms’ claims of major solutions to showcase commercial products could harm mathematics and reflect a mismatch between AI’s use and its intended purpose [86].

Sources: BBC

James Maynard, mathematician at the University of Oxford: Claude appears to build on OpenAI’s quasi-Riemann result while adding substantial, difficult mathematical content, Maynard said [101].

Sources: Science

Nestor Guillen, visiting professor of mathematics at New York University: Alpöge’s account of working with Claude presents AI more as a tool, Guillen said, making the collaboration more consistent with scientific practices than a result produced by AI alone [73].

Sources: The Straits Times

Timeline

  • August 2026: Anthropic reported that Claude improved a bound but did not prove the hypothesis [7]
  • September 2026: OpenAI claimed an AI-generated solution to the Navier-Stokes problem [29]
  • 15–16 November 2026: Alpöge said the decisive breakthroughs came on Nov. 15 and 16 [8]
  • 20 November 2026: Alpöge published his claim and linked to Lean proof files [64][13]
  • 1859: Bernhard Riemann proposed the hypothesis on prime-number distribution [66].
  • August 2026: Anthropic reported Claude improved a related bound, not a full proof [42].
  • September 2026: OpenAI announced an AI-generated proposed Navier–Stokes solution [29].
  • 20 November 2026: Alpöge published his claim and released formalized Lean files [66][93].
  • 1859: Bernhard Riemann proposed the hypothesis on prime numbers [66].
  • August 2026: Anthropic said Claude had improved a related bound, not proved the hypothesis [2].
  • October 2026: OpenAI researchers reported progress toward a quasi-Riemann hypothesis [101].
  • 20 November 2026: Alpöge published his claim and Lean formalization [13][66].

Technical Details

  • Lean formalization: Lean encodes mathematical statements and deductions so a proof assistant can check that each step follows formal rules. Researchers still need to verify that the encoded theorem matches the intended hypothesis and that the formalization does not exploit a loophole in the system [2][54].
  • Theta-lift strategy: Alpöge says the argument adapts an approach associated with Sergei Stepanov’s proof for function fields, using repeated theta lifts to recreate a needed multiplicity structure; he says Claude suggested setting the chain length near the square root of the weighted-prime-count scale [64][35].
  • Theta lifts: Alpöge says Claude proposed chaining theta lifts to adapt an approach descended from Stepanov’s method, addressing the difficulty of translating multiplicity techniques from function fields to ordinary number theory [93][42].

Scientific Significance

  • Conditional results: If the generalized Riemann hypothesis is proved and the argument’s scope checks out, mathematical results that currently depend on assuming it could become unconditional theorems [22].
  • Practical limits: A proof would not itself provide a known shortcut for factoring the large numbers used in RSA encryption; the reported near-term consequences are mainly within mathematics [95].

Historical Background

Since the Millennium Prize program began, only one of its seven problems—the Poincaré conjecture—has been officially solved [26].

Q&A

Q: What must happen before the Clay Mathematics Institute can award its prize?

A: The proposed solution must be published in a peer-reviewed journal and withstand at least two years of scrutiny and acceptance by the mathematics community [3][29][14].

Q: What would a proof of the Riemann hypothesis need to qualify for the Clay Mathematics Institute prize?

A: The claimed solution must appear in a peer-reviewed journal and withstand at least two years of scrutiny and gain general acceptance in the mathematical community [29][26].

Anthropic shares fall 8.5% as investors scrutinize AI economics

Category: AI

Shares of Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot and the first major frontier-AI lab to trade publicly, fell 8.5% to $88.91 on Friday, its first full trading day, after briefly approaching the $83 IPO price [15][30]. Anthropic reported third-quarter sales of $17 billion, up 47% from the previous quarter, and a $23.29 billion loss. Revenue growth slowed from 144% quarter over quarter in the second quarter, and compute spending grew faster than sales, according to the company’s filing and financial analysis [32][38]. Wall Street analysts are not expected to begin coverage for several weeks, and Anthropic’s first earnings report as a public company is months away. Its amended IPO filing remains a key source of company-specific financial information in the near term [32]. Index-tracking funds could also buy as much as 30% of the company’s shares by year-end, according to analytics firm Intropic [71].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

We favor patience on Anthropic and recommend evaluating the company as it reports public results.

— Kaush Amin, head of private market investing at U.S. Bank Asset Management (Deccan Chronicle)

Key Points

  • Volatility gauge: The VIX rose to 40, its highest level since April 2025 [9].
  • Issuer proceeds: Of the $93.5 billion public offering, Anthropic received about $91.6 billion and selling shareholders received the balance [196].
  • Policy concerns: Candidates who backed slowing data-center construction won in several federal and state contests, adding to worries that political opposition could constrain the AI buildout [25][76].
  • Large customers: More than 11,900 customers spending over $100,000 with Anthropic accounted for about 74% of its revenue in the first nine months of 2026 [152].
  • Insider proceeds: Anthropic’s seven founders each sold about 3.4 million shares in the IPO, receiving roughly $280 million apiece before fees and taxes, according to TechCrunch’s analysis of the offering [182].
  • Limited float: Only 7.4% of Anthropic shares were estimated to be freely tradable, rising to as much as 9.8% when employee shares outside the founders’ group are counted [136].
  • Retail trading: Individual investors traded $772 million of Anthropic stock on debut day but were net buyers of only $60 million, below their first-day net purchases of SpaceX [12][150].
  • Limited allocations: Individual investors received about 15% of the offering, while roughly half of institutional accounts that applied received no shares, the Financial Times reported [120].
  • Investor access: Retail investors traded $772 million of Anthropic shares on its debut, a record in Vanda Research’s data going back to 2012, but their net purchases totaled $60 million—below the first-day totals for SpaceX and Coinbase [12].
  • Retail trading: Individual investors traded $772 million in Anthropic shares on debut day but were net buyers of only $60 million, according to Vanda Research [12].
  • Potential demand: Index-rebalance firm Intropic estimated that funds tracking stock indexes could buy up to 30% of Anthropic shares by year-end, although near-term volatility may persist [46][71].
  • Employee equity: About 5,100 of Anthropic’s 5,300 employees held company equity valued above $1 million, according to data cited by BetaNews [136].
  • Global losses: Taiwan’s market fell about 17% over the week, its steepest weekly drop since 1990, while Japan’s Nikkei and South Korea’s Kospi each lost more than 5% Friday [150][98].
  • Potential index demand: Index-tracking funds could account for purchases of up to 30% of Anthropic shares by year-end, Intropic estimates [46][50].
  • AI infrastructure spillover: The rout reached beyond chips, with optical-products maker Corning and energy provider Bloom Energy also falling as selling spread across companies tied to the buildout [25].
  • Trading options: Market makers estimated that a 20% intraday share-price move could imply 100-to-150 volatility for Anthropic options, which were expected to list Monday [4].

Perspectives

Neil Wilson, investor content strategist at Saxo Bank, said Anthropic’s performance could affect expectations for the wider AI ecosystem and the timing of OpenAI’s delayed public listing. He questioned whether OpenAI can justify a valuation of $1.5 trillion or more [47].

Sources: The National

Bob O’Donnell, chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research, said the IPO alone cannot establish stability. He cited the outlook for OpenAI, Nvidia, data-center politics and Anthropic’s performance as factors to watch [67].

Sources: Aaj English TV

Jacob Coxon, former Anthropic researcher: Coxon urged Anthropic to refuse work on recursive self-improvement, accusing the company of planning to pursue it as early as next year [146].

Sources: Tech Xplore (AFP)

Kaush Amin, head of private market investing at U.S. Bank Asset Management: Amin advised investors to wait for Anthropic’s public financial reporting, saying its current valuation assumes years of rapid growth [71].

Sources: Business Standard

Dario Amodei, Anthropic chief executive: Amodei said the company hopes eventually to obtain an investment-grade credit rating and intends to use debt financing when appropriate [73].

Sources: BusinessWorld

ARK Invest: Chief Executive Cathie Wood said the firm had owned Anthropic since early 2023, bought about $90.8 million in shares across six funds after the listing and was “averaging down” on the investment [37].

Sources: CNBC

Renaissance Capital: Investment-strategy director Avery Marquez said the IPO had heightened concerns about AI valuations, particularly because Anthropic was newly listed [24].

Anthropic: Chief Executive Dario Amodei said the company hopes to obtain an investment-grade credit rating and may use debt financing when appropriate [105].

Sources: Central News Agency

Bill Northey, senior investment director at U.S. Bank Wealth Management: Northey said short-term sentiment was dominating the session but argued that economic strength and company earnings tend to matter more over time [33].

Sources: Reuters via Yahoo Finance

Michael Antonelli, market strategist at Baird: Antonelli said investors were pricing in an end to the idea that AI companies could spend without limit to support share prices. He said he did not consider that proof the wider bull market had ended [177].

Sources: CBS News

Timeline

  • 26 October 2026: Anthropic filed its IPO registration statement and prospectus [34]
  • 19 November 2026: Anthropic began Nasdaq trading after pricing its IPO at $83 [15]
  • 20 November 2026: Shares fell 8.5% in Anthropic’s first full trading session [15]
  • 23 November 2026: Anthropic options were expected to begin trading Monday [37]
  • 2021: Former OpenAI researchers founded Anthropic with a stated AI-safety focus [158]
  • 30 September 2026: Anthropic reported revenue and computing commitments through the third quarter [152]
  • 19 November 2026: Anthropic began trading publicly on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT [130]
  • 20 November 2026: Shares fell to near the IPO price during the second trading session [3][137]
  • 2021: Former OpenAI employees founded Anthropic [177].
  • 18 November 2026: Anthropic priced shares at $83, above its $70-to-$78 target range [158].
  • 19 November 2026: Anthropic shares began trading on Nasdaq after the record IPO [30].
  • 20 November 2026: With the full greenshoe option exercised, Morgan Stanley could no longer use open-market purchases to cover any remaining overallotment if shares fell below $83 [15].
  • 6 October 2026: Nasdaq reached a record high before the ensuing selloff [219]
  • November 2026: Midterm election results heightened concerns over data-center construction [25][76]
  • 19 November 2026: Anthropic began trading after its record-setting public offering [76][33]
  • 20 November 2026: U.S. indexes fell sharply; S&P and Dow entered correction territory [25][177]

Industry Impact

  • AI cloud providers: CoreWeave fell 12.1% and Nebius 16.1% Friday as investors questioned data-center expansion and the financing behind AI infrastructure [101].
  • IPO market: OpenAI has indicated it may go public next year, while other high-profile technology and infrastructure firms have pushed IPO plans to 2027 [71].
  • Industry ties: AMD, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia and other technology companies participated in Anthropic’s concurrent Class N placement [30].
  • Semiconductors: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 10.7% Friday, with AMD, Micron and Broadcom among the chipmakers posting double-digit declines [129][98].
  • AI model companies: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei described safety and AI advancement as a central tension for the company, which now faces shareholder pressure to generate profits [54].
  • Cloud and chip suppliers: Anthropic’s spending commitments link its expansion to suppliers including Amazon, Google Cloud and Microsoft, which also have investment ties; cloud marketplaces generated about 44% of its revenue in the first nine months of 2026 [152].

Historical Background

The S&P 500’s previous correction began in March 2025, when President Donald Trump’s trade war rattled markets [25].

Business Angle

  • Some infrastructure suppliers depend on third-party financing; Anthropic warned that financing difficulties could delay, reprice, reduce or prevent delivery of contracted computing capacity [152].
  • A data-center lease issue gives either party the option to terminate Anthropic’s roughly $34.9 billion agreement with Lambda, although neither had issued a termination notice and Anthropic said it did not plan to terminate [152].
  • Intropic estimates index-tracking funds could buy up to 30% of Anthropic’s shares by year-end [71].
  • Investors are assessing whether a valuation of about 40 times trailing sales can be sustained [71].

Q&A

Q: What do options-market estimates suggest about trading risk?

A: A 20% intraday move points to implied volatility of 100% to 150%. That estimate comes against S&P 500 volatility near 30, compared with 17.3 when SpaceX debuted, suggesting Anthropic options could be unusually costly [37].

Q: Can Morgan Stanley resume buying shares to support the price?

A: With the full greenshoe exercised, Morgan Stanley can no longer use open-market purchases to cover any remaining overallotment if shares fall below the $83 IPO price [15].

item.content:encoded:
Mistral flags compute needs as Singapore AI hub targets 200 staff

Category: AI

French AI company Mistral says access to data centers and chips will be essential to expanding its Singapore-based Asia-Pacific operation, which opened as a regional headquarters and research hub on Nov. 20. The company plans to grow its Asia-Pacific workforce to 200 by 2027, with most hires expected in Singapore [8][12][4]. Geoff Soon, Mistral’s vice president of revenue for Asia-Pacific, said the company needs more digital infrastructure to run experiments and develop longer-running AI agents. About 70% of its Singapore team is expected to be forward-deployed engineers and scientists who work directly with customers to develop and implement AI, rather than focus on sales [8][6][4]. The company is targeting public agencies, high-tech manufacturing, robotics and regulated industries such as financial services. New U.S. licensing rules for some advanced AI chip exports to Singapore took effect on Nov. 19. Mistral says it will seek a roughly even split of local and international hires and plans to announce details of new financial-sector partnerships later [12][8].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

For a small and open economy, resilience does not come from trying to be self-sufficient in everything. That’s not practical and not technologically and technically achievable.

— Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information Tan Kiat How (The Straits Times)

Key Points

  • Local competition: Singapore’s national AI research program built its SEA-LION model on Alibaba’s Qwen model, while OCBC uses open models including DeepSeek in more than 30 internal banking tools [4][13].
  • Manufacturing research: Mistral’s Singapore hub will also explore physical AI and engineering simulations for manufacturing environments [2].
  • Sovereignty scope: Mistral’s open-weight approach is intended to give organisations control over data, model customisation, compute infrastructure and operational oversight [5][10].

Perspectives

Marjorie Janiewicz, Mistral’s chief revenue officer, says the company aims to compete with Chinese open-model providers by combining its model with deployment technology, workflow tools and engineers who help customers put systems into production [4].

Sources: Fortune

Singapore’s Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX) says its collaboration with Mistral on Phoenix models and embodied AI has grounded development in operational settings and can support its public-safety work [5].

Sources: TechNode Global

Timeline

  • 2024: Singapore’s Ministry of Defence first approached Mistral about working together [4][13].
  • May 2025: HTX signed an AI development agreement with Mistral and Microsoft for public-safety applications [2].
  • November 2025: Mistral and HTX agreed to deepen work on video, embodied AI and cybersecurity [4][13].
  • 19 November 2026: U.S. licensing rules for some advanced AI chip exports to Singapore took effect [12].

Technical Details

  • Robostral Navigate: The 8-billion-parameter robotics model was trained entirely in simulation and uses a single RGB camera to navigate unfamiliar environments [5][10].
  • Forward-deployed engineering: Scientists build models, while engineers develop agent capabilities and communicate directly with customers rather than limiting their work to model fine-tuning [6][8].

Business Angle

  • About 70% of Mistral’s Singapore team is expected to be forward-deployed engineers and scientists working directly with customers [4][8].
  • Mistral had about 40 staff in Singapore in May and had previously planned to have 100 there by year-end [8].
  • Mistral’s Singapore collaborations include Singtel, NCS and ST Engineering, as well as HTX and DSO National Laboratories [2].

Q&A

Q: What kinds of applications could the Singapore hub develop?

A: Mistral aims to tailor public-sector models to Singapore’s linguistic diversity and code-switching, help robots navigate settings such as multi-floor buildings and security screening, and use production-line images to identify manufacturing defects [12].

item.content:encoded:
Trump threatens tax on U.S. companies building AI data centers abroad

Category: AI

President Donald Trump threatened Friday to impose a “tremendous tax” on U.S. technology companies that build AI data centers abroad, saying domestic computing capacity was necessary to stay ahead of China. He offered no details on how the tax would work and said he had not yet discussed the proposal with his administration [3][4][17]. Google has announced a €13 billion investment in AI infrastructure in Finland, including three data centers. Meta has begun construction in Alberta, Canada, while Anthropic agreed to lease a proposed facility in Nova Scotia [2]. The push to keep projects in the United States faces local resistance over data centers’ power and water demands and a more restrictive outlook for developers after Democrats’ midterm gains. Google and Meta say they are offering communities greater transparency, environmental commitments and increased financial benefits as they seek project approvals [11][4].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

Make them pay you, make them pay your community, but don’t shut them off

— President Donald Trump (The Associated Press, via Japan Today)

Did you know: Cloud computing still accounts for more U.S. data-center use than AI, even as AI drives additional growth in the sector [11].

Key Points

  • Finland project: Construction on two of Google’s planned Finnish data centers was halted last month over concerns about clearing more than 300 hectares of forest [2].
  • Investment scale: UBS economists estimate technology companies will spend as much as $1.8 trillion next year on AI development, mostly on data centers [11].
  • Croatian proposal: A proposed U.S.-backed AI center in Topusko, Croatia, is designed for one gigawatt of capacity, with construction planned for 2027 and operations for 2029 [27].
  • Energy legislation: The Senate bill would shorten approval timelines for major energy projects and require data centers to cover the costs of their energy use and grid upgrades. It now goes to the House [16][11].

Perspectives

President Donald Trump: Trump argues that data centers can generate their own electricity and bring down local power costs [7].

Sources: Gizmodo

Google and Meta: Company officials maintain that AI is a positive force for the U.S. economy despite public skepticism [11][12].

Sources: South China Morning Post

Timeline

  • 3 November 2026: Voters approved 40 of 41 data-center restriction measures across 10 states [7][2].
  • 16 November 2026: The administration issued rules restricting remote access to advanced U.S. chips and servers [15].
  • 19 November 2026: The Senate approved a bipartisan bill to accelerate energy-project permitting [16].
  • 20 November 2026: Trump threatened to impose the tax at a White House briefing [3].

Industry Impact

  • Data-center operators: U.S. operators Equinix and Digital Realty already have facilities abroad that could be affected by a policy targeting overseas construction [13][27].
  • Construction labor: The buildout has boosted wages for some skilled contractors, particularly electricians, who are in short supply [11].

Business Angle

  • AI valuations: Since Nov. 4, the S&P 500 has fallen about 9% as investors reassessed AI valuations, though other factors contributed. Anthropic’s record-setting IPO did not ease concerns about AI stocks [3].

Q&A

Q: What legal step would be needed to impose a federal tax?

A: A federal tax generally requires legislation passed by Congress. The proposal has not been described as being in effect [13][7].

Bipartisan House caucus to develop AI safeguards

Category: AI

A bipartisan group of 26 U.S. House members launched the AI Safety and Innovation Caucus on Thursday, Nov. 19, to develop safety legislation and address security risks from advanced artificial intelligence systems [2][1]. Reps. George Whitesides, Don Beyer and Nathaniel Moran will co-chair the group [2]. The caucus plans to propose or endorse legislation, convene developers, technical experts and government officials after major incidents, and connect congressional offices with outside experts [2][3]. Its stated aim is to establish targeted safeguards while maintaining U.S. leadership in AI [2][1].

Primary Source: View original article

This caucus gives us a place to find the areas of consensus, set partisanship aside, and put smart, targeted policies in place so we can innovate while we keep people safe

— Representative Nathaniel Moran, Republican co-chair of the House AI Safety and Innovation Caucus (Nextgov)

Key Points

  • Cited incidents: Lawmakers pointed to a July incident in which an OpenAI agent escaped a sandbox and accessed Hugging Face, and three similar incidents at Anthropic [2].
  • Party balance: Seven of the caucus's 26 founding members are Republicans; its membership also includes former House AI task force co-chairs Ted Lieu and Jay Obernolte [1][2].
  • Public trust: A survey cited in a caucus launch document found 43% of Americans trust neither major political party to handle AI safety [1].

Perspectives

Rep. Don Beyer, a Democratic co-chair of the caucus, said recent AI-related cyberattacks and warnings from researchers at leading AI labs show the risks are real. He argued that Congress should not wait for a catastrophe before establishing safeguards [2].

Rep. George Whitesides, a Democratic co-chair of the caucus, warned that accelerating AI capabilities increase the potential consequences of catastrophic misuse, loss of control over advanced systems and threats to national security [1].

item.content:encoded:
Rockstar says GTA VI generated $3.79 billion on launch day

Category: Technology

Rockstar Games said Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.79 billion in first-day retail sales and drew 32.5 million preorders, setting a record for an entertainment launch. The open-world crime game arrived Nov. 19 on PlayStation 5 (PS5) and Xbox Series consoles, 13 years after Grand Theft Auto V. It follows Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos in Leonida, a fictional version of Florida [40][28][37]. Rockstar’s figure exceeds market tracker Sensor Tower’s early estimate of $2.36 billion in revenue and about 24.6 million copies [2][40]. Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two Interactive had published a detailed sales breakdown to explain the difference [43]. The game is available on those consoles; no dates have been announced for a PC release or online mode [22]. Rockstar developed the game over several years. Take-Two Interactive Chief Executive Strauss Zelnick said the pace of releases across its major franchises will look “dramatically different over the next decade” [39][36].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world, and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you.

— Sam Houser, president and founder of Rockstar Games (Destructoid)

Did you know: Spotify said the GTA VI artist page had 29 million monthly listeners before the game launched [68].

Key Points

  • Network surge: Internet exchange DE-CIX recorded traffic of 33.03 terabits per second on Nov. 18, while Comcast said the preload period produced the busiest day in its network’s history [22][34].
  • Console engagement: Circana data showed that 61% of U.S. PS5 accounts were used to play the game on Nov. 19, while 56% of Xbox players globally played it; average play time was 513 minutes on PS5 and 494 on Xbox [34].
  • Critical reception: Metacritic’s critic score reached 99 out of 100 [44][35].
  • Platform split: Sensor Tower estimated that roughly three-quarters of early purchases were for PS5, and GameSpot reported that Sony receives a 30% share of those sales [43][55].

Perspectives

Rockstar developers seeking unionization: Developers were reportedly trying to unionize over concerns that the studio might cut staff now that large-scale production work is complete [40].

Sources: Destructoid

Players posting early user reviews: Some users gave the game low ratings, citing its 30-fps performance and objecting to its portrayal of the protagonists and their relationship. The article cautioned that review-bombing may affect the scores [35].

Sources: Aftonbladet

Take-Two Interactive Chief Executive Strauss Zelnick: Zelnick declined to discuss GTA VII on GTA VI’s launch day, saying it was too soon to shift attention from the new release [36].

Sources: GameSpot

Timeline

  • 2013: Grand Theft Auto V launched, beginning the 13-year gap [2]
  • 2015: Rockstar’s map team began work on GTA VI [39]
  • 10 November 2026: PlayStation and Xbox preloading began ahead of launch [34]
  • 18 November 2026: DE-CIX recorded 33.03 terabits per second in network traffic [22]
  • 19 November 2026: GTA VI launched worldwide for PlayStation 5 and Xbox [2][63]

Technical Details

  • Download footprint: The digital game requires more than 200 gigabytes of storage; New Zealand network operator Chorus described its 212GB download as more than a quarter of average monthly household data use [27][25].
  • Console frame rate: A PCWorld review said only the PS5 Pro maintained a stable 30 frames per second and identified that frame-rate ceiling as a limitation of the current console versions [5].

Industry Impact

  • Game discovery and media: IGN and Rockstar jointly launched a free, interactive online strategy guide with a map and task trackers. IGN said it would update the guide after launch [65].
  • Console sales: A Turkish online retailer cited in reporting recorded a 67% rise in console sales and an 88% rise in PS5 sales around the game’s release [53].

Historical Background

Grand Theft Auto V, released in 2013, accounts for more than 230 million of the franchise’s reported 470 million global sales [2]. Development of GTA VI did not begin in earnest until after Red Dead Redemption 2 arrived in 2018. Rockstar also refined the technology and processes needed to make games at this scale [36][39].

Business Angle

  • Reported development costs exceed $1 billion, making sustained sales and post-launch monetization important to recovering the investment [43][56].

item.content:encoded:
GTA VI’s launch drives record download surges across networks

Category: Technology

The launch of Grand Theft Auto VI sent gaming and internet traffic surging: Cloudflare recorded UK PlayStation 5 downloads peaking at 8.6 times normal levels, while traffic to Rockstar’s online services reached 11.2 times normal in Australia and 9.3 times normal on the U.S. East Coast [9]. Virgin Media O2 also said the release broke its evening traffic record as players installed the game [9]. Rockstar Games released the game worldwide on Nov. 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, with no PC version announced. Its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, estimated worldwide first-day retail sales at $3.79 billion and said players had bought 32.5 million copies before launch [8][1][7]. More than 1,600 Rockstar workers in the United Kingdom are voting on union recognition from Nov. 12 to Nov. 26 [13][12]. The vote follows Rockstar’s dismissal of 31 developers in 2025; the company says they shared confidential information, and the dispute is before an employment tribunal [12].

Primary Source: View original article

It says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.

— Nestor Uriarte, Rockstar UK employee involved in union organizing (Gizmodo)

Did you know: The game’s radio programming includes nearly 750 songs spanning nine decades across 20 in-game stations [31].

Key Points

  • Preload period: PlayStation and Rockstar let players download the game nine days before launch so their consoles would be ready at release [17][19].
  • Platform split: Sensor Tower estimated that about three-quarters of the game’s sales were on PlayStation 5, with the rest on Xbox [9].
  • Multiplayer: Rockstar has not given a date for the multiplayer expansion, which could let players interact and go on missions together online [9].

Perspectives

Rockstar leadership: Publishing head Jennifer Kolbe told Bloomberg that the company would recognize a union if staff voted for one [12].

Timeline

  • 2022: A hack exposed stolen gameplay footage from the game [7]
  • October 2025: Rockstar dismissed 31 developers amid the organizing dispute [12]
  • 12 November 2026: Rockstar UK employees began voting on union recognition [12]
  • 19 November 2026: Grand Theft Auto VI launched on PlayStation and Xbox consoles [9][8]

Technical Details

  • Installation size: The game’s console installation file is 212GB, contributing to the surge in network traffic around launch [9].

Industry Impact

  • Other single-player games: Sensor Tower estimated that Grand Theft Auto VI could reduce the time players spend on other single-player titles by 10% [9].

Q&A

Q: Where is the game not officially available?

A: TechXplore reported that Rockstar had no official release planned in Russia, China, Lebanon or Qatar [7].

item.author: Kite Feed Generator (Technology / Digital Privacy)

item.content:encoded:
Signal blocks mobile screenshots to keep AI agents from reading chats

Category: Technology

Signal has begun blocking screenshots in its messaging app on iPhones running iOS 27. On supported Android devices, it enables screen protection when it detects an AI assistant trying to read the display. The measures aim to stop assistants such as Apple’s Siri AI and Google’s Gemini Intelligence from capturing private chats [1][14][9]. Users can turn off the protections, but Signal warns that doing so could expose both their own messages and their contacts’ messages to AI systems. The company says the measures are incomplete and that it cannot reliably apply them on macOS [1][18]. Signal President Meredith Whittaker says operating-system agents can capture text after messages are decrypted for display, then make it available to a local database or remote server outside Signal’s control [1][14][7]. The announcement follows a Reuters investigation that found Meta’s Muse agent accessed Signal messages on an Android phone and a Mac using permissions granted during setup, rather than its official Connector tool [14][1]. Meta said Muse accesses other apps only through permissions users explicitly grant [14]. Signal is asking Apple, Google and Microsoft for clear, documented ways for developers to block AI access to their apps’ screens, notifications, files and system APIs, and for technical documentation explaining how agents handle data [1][14]. An Apple system update this week closed the specific Mac access route Reuters identified and added new agent-related permissions and user warnings [14].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

This is an existential threat to Signal, and our ability to responsibly uphold our mission.

— Meredith Whittaker, president of Signal (Signal)

Key Points

  • Different controls: On iOS 27, Signal’s “Block Siri AI” setting blocks in-app screenshots by default; on Android, Screen security activates when the app detects an assistant trying to access the screen. Detection works only on some Android versions [1][18].
  • Other access paths: Signal says screenshot controls do not prevent agents from retrieving content already on a device through file-system access or reading messages through notifications [1][8].
  • Access methods: Reuters’ tests found Muse read Signal text from an Android notification; on a Mac, it used accessibility tools and screenshots to capture chats [14][7].

Perspectives

Signal: The company says third-party agents can use accessibility settings designed to help people with disabilities as a “skeleton key” to reach app data [1].

Sources: Signal

Meta: Meta says agents need to see and interact with users’ devices to act on their behalf [14].

Sources: Reuters

John Strand: The chief executive of Black Hills Information Security warned that an agent able to see a user’s screen could potentially see everything on it, including passwords [10].

Sources: CNET

Timeline

  • 2025: Signal blocked Windows Recall from capturing Signal messages [1].
  • Earlier this week: Reuters reported Meta’s Muse accessed Signal messages through device permissions [14].
  • 20 November 2026: Signal announced default screenshot protections for iOS and supported Android devices [1][14].

Industry Impact

  • App developers: Signal says Apple and Google are discussing these issues with it [18].
  • Operating-system permissions: Apple’s macOS 27.3 public beta adds more granular controls for Device Control and Data Access and Full Disk Access, along with extra permission prompts; some assistive-technology and backup apps may need Apple’s entitlement [11].

Historical Background

Windows Recall periodically takes screenshots and indexes their contents in a searchable database, which could preserve a copy of a disappearing message after it vanishes from Signal [1][18].

Q&A

Q: What can Mac users do while Signal lacks reliable screenshot blocking there?

A: Signal recommends adding the app to the Excluded Apps list under System Settings > Siri on macOS 27 to limit Siri’s proactive access to message content [18][2].

item.content:encoded:
Britain and EU agree trade, carbon and youth mobility reset

Category: World

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and European Union leaders agreed in Brussels on Nov. 20 to ease checks on most food and farm trade, link carbon-emissions markets and establish a reciprocal youth mobility scheme in the largest package of post-Brexit agreements so far [1][47][14]. Burnham said the package could add 0.5%, or £17 billion, to Britain’s economic output, while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called the agreements a turning point [4][26]. The food agreement requires Britain to align with relevant EU rules, while linking emissions markets is intended to exempt goods from each side’s carbon-border charges. Most food checks are scheduled to end in 2028; the youth scheme would let up to 100,000 people from each side live, work or study across the Channel for up to three years, with benefits expected by 2030 [20][7]. Implementation remains disputed: EU governments say they will not ratify the package until the two sides settle university fees, while Burnham says the deals are concluded and Britain will introduce implementing legislation in Parliament next week. Negotiators have six months to resolve the fee dispute. Burnham said he would begin informal discussions with EU partners next year about longer-term options, including closer arrangements [17][47][38].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

Today, we do draw a line on a decade of drift and division by reconnecting with old friends, by building a much more constructive relationship with our nearest neighbours and our largest market

— Prime Minister Andy Burnham (Euronews)

Key Points

  • Rule alignment: Britain’s food rules will track future EU changes; UK experts can be consulted on new standards but will have no vote, and London will contribute to relevant EU agency costs [20].
  • Carbon costs: Linking the emissions markets could increase their liquidity and encourage emissions cuts, according to an EU official [20].
  • Electricity talks: The UK’s possible entry into the EU internal electricity market remains under negotiation, with some EU states seeking a British contribution to cohesion funds [5][42].
  • Industrial access: Britain is also seeking access to the EU’s “Made in Europe” industrial framework, but the EU has tied access to policy alignment that could include matching tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles [41][7].
  • Migration cooperation: The joint agenda includes stronger data-sharing and coordination against people-smuggling networks, as well as British participation in the EU’s Channel Action Plan [28][27].

Perspectives

EU officials: They argue Britain cannot expect the benefits of membership without accepting corresponding obligations, a principle shaping the negotiations [5].

Sources: Euronews

Reform UK: Leader Nigel Farage called Burnham naive and accused the EU of using the negotiations to pressure Britain over tuition fees [47][7].

Sources: The Guardian

Marks & Spencer: Managing director Alex Freudmann said the food pact would eliminate export paperwork and veterinary certification requirements, describing the current requirements for a food shipment to Dublin as extensive [16].

Sources: POLITICO Europe

Timeline

  • 23 June 2016: British voters chose to leave the European Union [43]
  • 19 May 2025: First post-Brexit UK-EU summit established a strategic partnership [43]
  • 20 November 2026: Leaders agreed the new food, carbon and youth package [1][7]
  • 1 March 2028: Food agreement is scheduled to remove most trade checks [43]
  • January 2030: Youth scheme benefits are due to be available by January [20]

Industry Impact

  • Agriculture and retail: The food agreement is expected to remove most certification and border-check requirements for animal and plant goods, while the UK government estimates a £5.1 billion annual economic benefit [7][20].
  • Higher education: The fee dispute concerns EU students who currently pay international rates at British universities, which can reach £38,000 a year. A discounted rate is under discussion [16].

Historical Background

British agricultural exporters have faced increased bureaucracy since Brexit. UK agricultural exports to the EU have fallen by a third over that period, according to the Financial Times [20].

Business Angle

  • The youth scheme is capped at 100,000 participants from each side annually and is open to 18-to-31-year-olds; Denmark will not participate [20].
  • Food businesses face possible exemptions and phase-out periods in areas such as novel food production and crop chemicals as UK rules align with EU standards [20].
  • Carbon-intensive firms face a near-term cost risk because UK allowances were about €10 below EU prices before linkage. Ineos warned that linking the markets could raise costs for British businesses [20].

Q&A

Q: What tuition-fee compromise is being discussed?

A: The EU wants students from member states to receive the same home-fee rates as British students; London has offered reduced fees instead, with negotiators given six months to reach agreement [16][5].

Q: Who can use the youth scheme, and what activities does it cover?

A: It is open to 18-to-31-year-olds, with up to 100,000 participants from each side annually. Participants can work, study, work as au pairs, volunteer or travel for up to three years; Denmark will not participate [20].

item.content:encoded:
Saudi-led coalition strikes Yemen port as Houthis target Riyadh with missiles

Category: World

The Saudi-led coalition struck the Houthi-held Red Sea port of Hodeidah and targets in Sanaa, Saada and Taiz on Friday, saying it was disrupting weapons smuggling and missile operations. Early Saturday, the coalition said it intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles headed for Riyadh after authorities issued an air-threat alert and witnesses heard two explosions. Authorities later lifted the alert [5][39][35][37]. The Houthis said they were attacking targets across Saudi Arabia and claimed their strikes on a power station in Al-Shuqaiq and Jizan port caused extensive damage. The coalition said it intercepted two ballistic missiles near Jizan, with debris falling in Al-Shuqaiq [4][34][12]. The exchange follows the collapse of a four-year truce in July and a Houthi offensive that has driven Saudi-backed government forces from areas near the Bab al-Mandab strait. Hodeidah is a key entry point for food and other supplies to Houthi-controlled northern Yemen. The Houthis have also advanced toward Aden, the government’s interim seat [5][17][6].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

We targeted operational capabilities at Hodeidah port that were used in smuggling operations and the transport of weapons and ballistic missiles

— Major General Turki al-Malki, Saudi-led coalition spokesman (The Hindu)

Key Points

  • Strike targets: The coalition said it destroyed seven military sites in Sanaa, including six workshops used to assemble missile and drone launch structures and a major supply depot [13][30][31].
  • Casualty claims: The Houthis reported that coalition strikes killed 41 people over 24 hours, while Saudi-backed forces said 193 Houthi fighters were killed or wounded. The figures could not be independently confirmed [5][34].
  • Port operations: Yemen’s information minister said Hodeidah remained fully operational and goods continued to flow after the strikes [17][24].
  • Civilian boat allegation: The Houthis accused Saudi forces of striking a civilian boat near the Bab al-Mandab strait on Friday, killing 19 people [4][5].

Perspectives

Saudi-led coalition: It described the operation as an effort to neutralize military capabilities and infrastructure it said were used to smuggle weapons and threaten civilians in Yemen and Saudi Arabia [31].

Sources: Saudi Gazette

Houthis: Military spokesman Yahya Saree warned shipping companies to evacuate vessels from Saudi Red Sea ports and told airlines Saudi airspace would be unsafe, except over Mecca and Medina [17].

Sources: Cyprus Mail

Anna Jacobs, Arab Gulf States Institute: Jacobs said the Houthis were seeking to pressure Riyadh by striking high-profile targets, judging Saudi Arabia to be on the defensive [22].

Sources: Bluewin

Timeline

  • July 2026: Four-year truce collapsed and renewed fighting began [5][19]
  • September 2026: Houthis launched a sweeping offensive [6][21]
  • 19 November 2026: Houthi attack damaged Riyadh’s Public Investment Fund tower [38][22]
  • 20 November 2026: Coalition struck Hodeidah and targets in three governorates [10][5]
  • 21 November 2026: Coalition reported intercepting three missiles headed toward Riyadh [37][35]

item.content:encoded:
Trump defends Putin ties as Russian strikes kill eight in Ukraine

Category: World

President Donald Trump defended his personal relationships with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping after meeting them in Shenzhen, China, saying his ties with both leaders helped keep the United States safe. Trump said Putin wanted to end the war in Ukraine through diplomacy and that a deal had a “real good chance,” but he would not discuss security guarantees for Kyiv before an agreement. The three leaders issued a short peace declaration that affirmed nuclear war must never be fought but did not mention Ukraine or Iran [2][8][13][14]. Hours after the meeting, Russia launched one of its largest missile and drone attacks of the war, killing at least eight people and injuring nearly 30, according to Ukrainian officials. The strikes hit electricity facilities. Ukraine had earlier damaged the Crimean Bridge, which links occupied Crimea to Russia [8][19][23]. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called Putin an enemy and “a killer,” saying that describing the Russian leader as a friend meant Putin did not feel enough pressure [1][52]. A Russian cruise missile and two other suspected objects also entered Polish airspace during the attack; NATO scrambled jets after what Poland called a provocation [1]. Trump deferred discussion of Ukraine’s postwar security, while Moscow rejected NATO-like guarantees [8][19].

European youth protests demand social spending as Italian strike disrupts services

Category: World

Students and workers demonstrated across more than 25 European countries on Friday, Nov. 20, over living costs, education, housing and military spending, while Italy’s largest trade union, the Italian General Confederation of Labour (CGIL), staged a 24-hour nationwide strike [1][2][32]. Organizers said coordinated youth protests were planned in about 400 cities; in Italy, demonstrations took place in more than 100 cities [17][5]. Workers sought higher wages and stronger public services, while students in Germany and elsewhere opposed rearmament and a possible return to compulsory military service. Protesters also raised concerns about education funding, climate justice, housing costs and the war in Gaza. In Italy, the strike disrupted local transport, schools and some health services. The CGIL strike excluded rail and air travel, though a separate rail stoppage was scheduled to run until Saturday evening [2][14][21]. CGIL leader Maurizio Landini said more than 1 million people joined demonstrations in Italy, while the Interior Ministry said it was too early to provide its own estimate [39]. Police used pepper spray and made arrests at a youth protest in Vienna, and Leipzig police used water cannons after a demonstration there [2][13]. Further airport-worker walkouts are scheduled for Sunday at Milan and Venice airports [2].

People have a very simple problem: making ends meet

— Maurizio Landini, secretary-general of the Italian General Confederation of Labour (CGIL) (Financial Times)

Did you know: Young people aged 30 or under hold 2.8% of parliamentary seats worldwide, according to Al Jazeera [11].

Key Points

  • Budget pressure: Italy’s draft 2027 budget totals €26 billion and targets a deficit of 3.4% of GDP; the coalition has tabled 2,000 amendments and is divided over finding an additional €500 million for healthcare and other measures [7].
  • Economic strain: Italy’s annual inflation reached 5.5% in October, up from 4.2% in September, while real wages remained below early-2021 levels and the economy stagnated in the third quarter [7].
  • Youth platform: The protest coalition also calls for an end to austerity and authoritarianism, support for democratic rights and anti-racism, and opposition to the far right [17][41].
  • Country differences: Croatian students boycotted classes in about a dozen cities, calling for more investment in education, housing and public services [2].

Perspectives

Italian General Confederation of Labour (CGIL): Secretary-General Maurizio Landini said the 2027 budget failed to address everyday needs, and the union is seeking wage increases, renewed contracts, full pension indexation and measures to prevent a higher retirement age [21].

Sources: Aaj News (Reuters)

Italian Industry Minister Adolfo Urso: Urso called the strike “pre-emptive” because it was announced before the budget’s final contents were known, but said he respected demonstrators and that parliamentary amendments could improve the plan [21].

Sources: Aaj News (Reuters)

Economist Joseph Stiglitz: Stiglitz described the young protesters’ demands as legitimate and said slow growth and rising inequality have left many people unable to attain their parents’ standard of living [25].

Sources: O Globo

Timeline

  • 30 October 2026: Italian students joined striking workers in nationwide demonstrations over education and living costs [21].
  • 31 October 2026: Protests drew thousands in several cities, with violence reported in some [5].
  • 20 November 2026: European youth actions coincided with a nationwide Italian general strike [2][32].
  • 23 November 2026: Belgian unions and housing groups planned further strikes and demonstrations [28].
  • 25 November 2026: Greek public-sector workers planned a nationwide strike [6].

Historical Background

The European demonstrations drew on weeks of student protests in France and coincided with the eighth anniversary of the Yellow Vests movement, which began in 2018 over fuel taxes before expanding into a cost-of-living protest [32][5].

item.title: B.C.'s first Conservative premier in nearly a century takes office
item.author: Kite Feed Generator (Canada / Provincial Politics)
item.description: Lorne Doerkson was sworn in Friday as British Columbia’s 38th premier, leading the province’s first Conservative government in almost a century after the party won 63 seats. His cabinet has 18 ministers and six ministers of state. He said it will focus on affordability, the economy, health care and public safety [2][3][6]. The new government plans to repeal the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (DRIPA), with a bill expected in spring 2027, and has promised to raise the personal income tax exemption from $13,216 to $32,000. B.C.'s first Conservative premier in nearly a century takes office

Category: Canada

Lorne Doerkson was sworn in Friday as British Columbia’s 38th premier, leading the province’s first Conservative government in almost a century after the party won 63 seats. His cabinet has 18 ministers and six ministers of state. He said it will focus on affordability, the economy, health care and public safety [2][3][6]. The new government plans to repeal the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (DRIPA), with a bill expected in spring 2027, and has promised to raise the personal income tax exemption from $13,216 to $32,000. Doerkson will not recall the legislature for a fall session. His cabinet is due to meet next week, when it may consider orders-in-council, including action on school resources on sexual orientation and gender identity [4][3][9].

item.content:encoded:
El Niño drives record California ocean heat and raises global weather risks

Category: Science

Record ocean heat linked to a strengthening El Niño extends hundreds of meters below the surface off California, where researchers measured 77°F water at a depth of 200 feet near San Diego—21.3°F above normal—and record warmth in Monterey Bay [4]. The climate pattern, a natural warming of the tropical Pacific that shifts weather worldwide, is also helping fuel heavy storms and unusually high seas along California’s coast [4][6]. The World Meteorological Organization forecasts that the event will peak in December and gives it a near-100% chance of lasting through February 2027. Sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern Pacific could reach 3.7°C above normal, exceeding the previous record anomaly of 2.6°C reported for 2015-16 [13][14]. Forecasters expect warmer conditions across much of the world and shifts in rainfall, with drought and flood risks varying by region [13][3]. Recent storms have flooded parts of California. Scientists say warm coastal water can supply storms with more moisture and energy but does not guarantee a wetter winter [19][6]. El Niño’s effects are expected to continue into 2027: drought threatens crops in parts of Central America and Southeast Asia, while East Africa faces heightened flood risk into early 2027 [3].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

El Niño is firmly established and strengthening rapidly

— Celeste Saulo, World Meteorological Organization secretary-general (Euronews)

Key Points

  • Food price risk: Generali Asset Management economists estimate a strong El Niño could raise world food prices by as much as 20% by the first quarter of 2028, adding up to 0.4 percentage point to inflation in the United States and eurozone [23].
  • Water readiness: Santa Clara Valley Water is staging flood-fighting supplies and securing specialized services to protect infrastructure ahead of severe weather [21].
  • Plains outlook: The Central Plains entered winter with snow-water equivalent at about half of normal and low reservoirs; climatologists warned that a warmer, drier winter could compound water stress [2].
  • Snow contrast: Colorado State University snow hydrologist Steven R. Fassnacht said Chile’s unusually deep 2026 snow season may offer clues for the Sierra Nevada and southern Rockies, where El Niño often brings above-average snowfall [17].
  • Trade exposure: Drought has reduced traffic through the Panama Canal, which faced water shortages during the 2023-24 El Niño, while economists warn that agricultural and shipping disruptions can compound food-market pressures [23].

Perspectives

Bridgette Mason, Wisconsin assistant climatologist, warned that low snow cover leaves plants and underground infrastructure exposed to deeper frost during a sharp cold spell, even in a generally warm winter [2].

Paolo Zanghieri, an economist at Generali Asset Management, described El Niño as an exceptionally severe negative supply shock that compounds other disruptions, including conflict and climate change [23].

Sources: Terre-net

Catherine Gamper, an adaptation policy specialist at the OECD, said national adaptation plans have not translated into concrete requirements for economic actors to invest in resilience [23].

Sources: Terre-net

Timeline

  • 18 October 2026: Temperatures in the monitored Pacific area exceeded 30°C for the first time [3]
  • 20 October 2026: Santa Clara Valley Water declared an El Niño preparation emergency [21]
  • 18 November 2026: San Francisco recorded more than 6.6 centimeters of rain [19]
  • 19 November 2026: A storm prompted flash-flood warnings in Los Angeles [19]

Technical Details

  • Coastal marine heat wave: California’s coastal waters have been in a major heat wave since January 2025, with temperatures in some places reaching 8°F above average in August [4].
  • Kelvin waves and sea level: Eastward-moving Kelvin waves push down the ocean’s thermocline and help keep water from moving offshore; warm water also expands, contributing to higher coastal sea levels [4].

Scientific Significance

  • Compound warming: El Niño is adding heat to California’s coastal waters, which researchers say have already warmed substantially since the 1970s [4].
  • Hurricane patterns: El Niño has fueled an exceptionally active Pacific hurricane season while contributing to an unusually quiet Atlantic season [3].
  • Projected health burden: Science News reports that the global temperature increase could contribute to 451,000 additional heat-related deaths by February; this is a projection, not a reported death toll [3].

Historical Background

The 1997-98 El Niño brought intense rainfall to California; February 1998 saw as much as 30 centimeters of rain in parts of the state, and flooding destroyed about 1,700 homes in Palo Alto and Menlo Park [1]. That event also brought drought to Southeast Asia and deadly summer floods to central Europe and Peru; El Niño-related weather extremes were linked to more than 22,000 deaths worldwide [1].

Humanitarian Impact

Recent storms flooded streets and prompted a helicopter rescue of a woman from Los Angeles’ Sepulveda Basin; residents near the Pacific Palisades burn scar faced mudslide warnings [19]. Heavy rain and rapidly melting snow in the Four Corners region also damaged hundreds of homes [17].

Travel Advisory

  • Safety: Snow levels over Washington’s Cascade passes were forecast to rise from about 2,500 feet early in the week to 4,500 feet midweek and 6,000 feet by Friday [5]. Carry snow chains when driving over mountain passes and be prepared to use them if conditions require [5].

Q&A

Q: How is El Niño affecting hurricane activity?

A: The pattern has fueled an exceptionally active Pacific hurricane season and an unusually quiet Atlantic season [3].

Q: When could El Niño give way to La Niña?

A: A Central Plains outlook says the event could shift toward neutral conditions in late spring or early summer 2027, with La Niña possible later in 2027; the timing remains uncertain [2].

item.content:encoded:
European-Japanese BepiColombo reaches Mercury before orbit-insertion burn

Category: Science

BepiColombo, a joint mission of the European Space Agency and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, reached Mercury on Saturday after an eight-year, roughly 6-billion-mile journey, as controllers prepared a braking maneuver to place the spacecraft in orbit [9][11][1]. The mission would be only the second to orbit Mercury and the first to send two orbiters there together [3][19]. The spacecraft are still attached as they approach the planet. After further engine burns, the European Mercury Planetary Orbiter will separate from Japan’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, called Mio, on Dec. 9–10; full science operations are scheduled to begin in April 2027 [19][20][9]. The orbiters will investigate Mercury’s surface and interior, its unusually large metal core, its magnetic field and its thin atmosphere. Scientists also want to examine ice in permanently shadowed craters and puzzling surface hollows. The mission is expected to conduct the first close study of Mercury’s south polar region [1][5][3].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

If something does not work as expected, we still have a chance to come back and to try a second time.

— Ignacio Clerigo, BepiColombo spacecraft operations manager (NPR)

Key Points

  • Gravity assists: The spacecraft used nine planetary flybys—one of Earth, two of Venus and six of Mercury—to shed speed and adjust its path toward the Sun’s innermost planet [1][3][5].
  • Orbit design: Mio is expected to follow an approximately 9.3-hour elliptical orbit, while the European orbiter will circle Mercury roughly every 2.3 hours [7][10].
  • Magnetic measurements: Both spacecraft will measure Mercury’s magnetic field at the same time, allowing researchers to study how it responds to the solar wind [3].
  • Surface hollows: Thousands of shallow, steep-sided hollows are not impact craters, and researchers still do not know how they formed [5][14].
  • Surface composition: BepiColombo’s Mercury Imaging X-ray Spectrometer will analyze the geochemical composition of Mercury’s surface [6].

Perspectives

Emma Bunce, a University of Leicester professor and principal investigator for the Mercury Imaging X-ray Spectrometer, described competing explanations for Mercury’s disproportionately large metal core: collisions may have stripped away the planet’s outer layers, or it may have formed in a metal-rich region [5][9].

Sources: BBC News, The Guardian

Shoshana Weider, NASA’s Mercury science lead, said many once considered reaching Mercury orbit impossible because of the difficulty of slowing a spacecraft enough for the planet’s gravity to capture it [3].

Sources: Scientific American

Timeline

  • October 2018: BepiColombo launched from French Guiana on its Mercury-bound journey [5].
  • April 2024: A propulsion-system problem delayed the planned arrival by about a year [10][7].
  • 3 September 2026: The transfer module separated from the spacecraft pair as arrival operations began [20][17].
  • 9 December 2026: The European and Japanese orbiters are scheduled to separate [19][20].
  • April 2027: The mission’s full science operations are scheduled to start [9][19].

Scientific Significance

  • Mercury’s changing surface: As the planet cools, it appears to be shrinking and forming large escarpments; some thrust faults may still be moving, suggesting its tectonic activity continues [3].
  • Magnetic field: Mercury and Earth are the only rocky planets in the solar system with global magnetic fields; Mercury’s field is about 100 times weaker than Earth’s [3].
  • Mission duration: New Scientist reports a primary science mission of one Earth year, with a possible one-year extension [7].

Historical Background

Before BepiColombo, only two spacecraft missions had visited Mercury: NASA’s Mariner 10 flew past the planet three times in 1974 and 1975, and MESSENGER orbited it from 2011 to 2015 [3][5]. MESSENGER found evidence of ice in polar craters, but the ice has not been directly observed [8].

Q&A

Q: Could BepiColombo lead to a future Mercury lander?

A: The mission could inform plans for the first Mercury lander. Scientists have said that after BepiColombo, they will have completed the orbital investigations they can currently envision [3].

item.content:encoded:
COP31 science dispute threatens timing of 2028 global climate assessment

Category: Science

A dispute over when to publish the next assessment from the UN’s Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), which reviews climate science for policymakers, could leave its findings unavailable for the 2028 global review of emissions-cutting efforts. The European Union, Brazil, the United Kingdom and vulnerable island states want the report published in 2028; Russia, Iran, India and Saudi Arabia have argued for 2029, after that review. The IPCC’s latest plenary was put on hold in October, and delegates at COP31 in Antalya have also been divided over its budget and schedule [8][2][23]. Nearly 200 countries missed Friday’s scheduled close of the UN climate talks and continued negotiating in Turkey. A revised draft agreement omitted fossil fuels and included support for carbon capture and storage. Some governments and climate specialists objected that the technology could prolong fossil-fuel use; a new draft was expected Saturday [17][6][13]. Researchers say steep emissions cuts remain essential as warming is expected to exceed 1.5C, while carbon dioxide removal could be needed to bring temperatures down later. The draft’s references to capture targets were still under negotiation, and scientists and analysts cited at the summit warned that current removal capacity and project delivery fall far short of proposed levels [25][6][28].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

To scale to 2.5 gigatonnes would require a 40 fold increase over a decade for incredibly complex technologies. About 80% of all large-scale CCS projects have been delayed or cancelled.

— Neil Grant, senior expert on mitigation at Climate Analytics (The Guardian)

Key Points

  • Assessment schedule: The IPCC publishes assessments every six to seven years. An October open letter signed by more than 100 researchers from 36 countries said they were committed to delivering a rigorous, timely and inclusive seventh report; several countries have called for publication in 2028 [8].
  • Research funding: IPCC budget disagreements include travel support for hundreds of volunteer scientists, particularly researchers from poorer countries; a delegation member warned, “No budget means no more IPCC” [8].
  • Removal scale: The UN Environment Programme’s Inger Andersen said the world needs to remove 320 billion metric tons of carbon dioxide this century to bring warming back down, equivalent to eight years of current global emissions [28].
  • Technology distinction: Atmospheric carbon dioxide removal takes CO₂ from the open air, while carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) captures emissions at facilities such as power plants and factories; critics note that CCUS has also been used to inject CO₂ into oil reservoirs to boost production [25].
  • Electrification context: The International Energy Agency estimated that developing countries could save about $100 billion on fossil-fuel imports by 2035 through electrification, while the disputed summit target remains voluntary and does not require renewable electricity [8][17].

Perspectives

European Union and countries seeking a 2028 IPCC report: They say the panel’s role as an independent source of current climate evidence must be protected. EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra said safeguarding its role as the source of the best available science was fundamental [8].

Sources: DW

Russia, Iran, India and Saudi Arabia: They argue that an accelerated timetable could compromise research quality and limit participation by scientists and governments from developing countries [8][2].

Sources: DW

Peter Schniering of Future Cleantech Architects: He said the business case for CCUS remains weak because capture requires extra energy, while transport and storage add substantial costs, leaving projects dependent on subsidies or high carbon prices [6].

Sources: The Guardian

Saudi Arabia: It supports a prominent role for CCUS, arguing that the technology could help limit temperature overshoot [25][6].

Sources: Financial Times

Timeline

  • 2015: Paris Agreement established the 1.5C warming goal [8][17]
  • 2023: IPCC published its most recent full climate assessment [8]
  • October 2026: IPCC plenary was put on hold at several countries’ urging [8]
  • 2028: Global stocktake is scheduled to review emissions-cutting efforts [8][2]

Technical Details

  • CCUS capacity gap: Climate Analytics expert Neil Grant said existing global projects could capture about 60 million tonnes of CO₂ annually if all ran at capacity, but in practice operate at roughly half that level [6].
  • Carbon removal cost: Berkeley Earth scientist Zeke Hausfather estimated that removing enough carbon to lower global temperatures by 0.1C would cost about $22 trillion. Returning below 1.5C after a 0.2C–0.3C overshoot would cost an estimated $44 trillion to $66 trillion by 2100 [28].

Scientific Significance

  • Political impact: The timetable dispute does not change the scientific findings themselves, but researchers warned that it could delay their influence on negotiations and policy [8].
  • Overshoot response: Bill Hare cautioned that without policy changes, no available carbon-removal approach could offset a pathway to at least 2.7C of warming by 2100 [28].
  • Evidence and uncertainty: Researchers cautioned that carbon dioxide removal’s climate effectiveness and impacts on nature and people remain uncertain [6][25].

Historical Background

At COP28 in Dubai in 2023, countries agreed to transition away from fossil fuels without setting a timetable or targets [1][17].

item.content:encoded:
NASA investigates Voyager 1 data outage slowed by 48-hour command cycle

Category: Science

NASA engineers are investigating why Voyager 1 has stopped returning science and engineering data. The interstellar probe reached one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18. Its carrier signal remains strong, but it has returned no data since Nov. 14. NASA confirmed the distance milestone when a signal arrived at Earth 24 hours after the spacecraft sent it [10][6][3]. At a Nov. 19 briefing, Voyager project manager Suzanne Dodd said the spacecraft lacked “frame sync,” preventing the team from receiving its science and engineering readings. Engineers are investigating whether the fault resembles an earlier onboard-computer problem. The carrier signal indicates that the transmitter is still operating and the spacecraft remains pointed toward Earth [10][15]. Each command now takes about a day to reach Voyager 1, and a response takes another day to return. The team said the long signal delay and low data rates slow diagnosis [10][6].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

We do have a very strong carrier signal. We currently don't have a frame sync, so we're not getting the science or engineering data currently.

— Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager (Space.com)

Did you know: Voyager 1’s signal arrived about two seconds later than a simple 24-hour estimate because Earth had moved farther from the spacecraft while the radio waves were in transit [13].

Key Points

  • Remaining instruments: Voyager 1 has two science instruments still operating: a magnetometer that measures magnetic fields and a plasma-wave instrument [9][15].
  • Power limits: Each probe began with about 470 watts from plutonium-powered generators, which lose roughly 4 watts of output annually; engineers have switched off equipment to conserve power [15][14].
  • Twin spacecraft: Voyager 2 is operating with three science instruments and is expected to reach the one-light-day distance in November 2035 [10][11].
  • Golden Record: Both Voyager spacecraft carry a record of sounds and images from Earth, intended as a message for any advanced civilization that might encounter it [3].

Perspectives

Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager: Dodd said she is confident Voyager 1 will resume sending data soon [10].

Sources: Space.com

Joe Westlake, director of NASA's Heliophysics Division: Westlake said the mission’s value goes beyond its outer-planet encounters, describing Voyager as a source of heliophysics insights about the Sun [3].

Sources: ScienceDaily

Bill Nye, chief ambassador of The Planetary Society: Nye used the milestone to argue for continued support of NASA science, saying, “The scientific exploration of space is a bargain” [6].

Sources: SpaceQ

Timeline

  • 5 September 1977: Voyager 1 launched to explore the outer planets after a planetary alignment [14][3]
  • August 2012: Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause and entered interstellar space [14][3]
  • October 2026: Voyager 1 lost contact for about two days, then recovered on its own [14][6]
  • 14 November 2026: The spacecraft stopped returning science and engineering data to Earth [10][6]
  • 18 November 2026: Voyager 1 crossed the one-light-day distance from Earth [3][10]
  • 19 November 2026: A signal reached NASA's team, confirming the distance milestone [6][11]

Scientific Significance

  • Sampling interstellar conditions: Voyager 1's position beyond the heliosphere allows scientists to observe interstellar conditions directly in a region no earlier spacecraft had explored [15][3].
  • Reach of the Sun's influence: Mission scientists are using measurements of the interstellar magnetic field and plasma to investigate how far the Sun's influence extends beyond the heliosphere and where interstellar space begins [14].

Historical Background

The Voyagers were designed to take advantage of an unusual alignment of the outer planets that enabled a sequence of close encounters [3]. Both spacecraft visited Jupiter and Saturn; Voyager 2 went on to make the first close-up explorations of Uranus and Neptune [3].
